content: 1. The planning and coordination of health-related activities should include prevention and mitigation strategies, preparedness and response measures, recovery planning, business continuity management, and exercise management. These efforts must be systematically organized and integrated into emergency risk management for health (ERMH) programs. 2. Information and knowledge management are critical components of ERMH. This includes conducting risk assessments, establishing early warning and surveillance systems, and promoting research to enhance emergency preparedness and response capabilities. 3. Health infrastructure and logistics must be robust and resilient. This involves ensuring the availability of essential supplies, maintaining safer and prepared health facilities, and implementing logistics systems to support health services during emergencies. 4. Health-care services must be adapted to meet the needs of affected populations during emergencies. This includes providing public health measures, specialized services for specific hazards, and maintaining essential non-hazard-related health services. 5. Community-based ERMH capacities should be strengthened by building local health workforce capabilities and fostering community-centered planning and action. 6. Pandemic influenza risk management plans must clearly define the roles, responsibilities, and authorities of responders. These roles should be documented with written terms of reference for each specific function. 7. Capacity development is essential to ensure that the health workforce is adequately trained and equipped to implement ERMH. This requires a thorough assessment of training needs and the development of effective training programs tailored to different target groups. 8. The World Health Organization (WHO) plays a key role in supporting policies and resource management. This includes helping countries assess and strengthen their core capacities to meet International Health Regulations (IHR) obligations, providing technical support for disease burden documentation, and advising on ethical frameworks for policy development. 9. WHO also supports the strengthening of global influenza surveillance and diagnostic capabilities, promotes the development of pandemic vaccines, and facilitates technology transfer to enhance vaccine production in developing countries. 10. Effective planning and coordination require the health sector to be represented at all levels of government in emergency risk management forums. This ensures that health needs are identified and technical advice is provided to other sectors. 11. Prevention and mitigation actions should be based on detailed risk assessments and integrated into ERMH programs at national and subnational levels. These measures must be coordinated with relevant technical departments and stakeholders across government, business, and civil society. 12. Recovery planning for the health sector should be given sufficient attention, with contingency plans and standard operating procedures developed, regularly updated, and tested well in advance of emergencies. 13. Communication strategies are vital throughout the ERMH continuum. National and local authorities must provide clear, timely, and transparent information to the public before, during, and after health emergencies to build trust and manage expectations. 14. Risk communication should facilitate the exchange of information among scientific, public health, and veterinary experts to support the assessment, implementation, and coordination of risk management activities. 15. Early warning and surveillance systems must be robust and capable of capturing critical data for assessing severity, implementing operational research protocols, and evaluating national impacts based on predefined criteria. 16. WHO provides technical guidance and support to member states in identifying priority needs, developing response strategies, and preparing for pandemic influenza risk management. This includes facilitating regional and cross-border collaborations. 17. Logistics and infrastructure management are essential for effective health emergency responses. This includes transportation, telecommunications, stockpiling, and distribution of medicines and supplies, as well as the establishment of temporary health facilities. 18. The Ministry of Health should make advance arrangements with government departments, external agencies, and private companies to ensure logistical support during emergencies. This includes identifying and training operational and logistics response teams. 19. Health services during emergencies must prioritize triage, emergency care, and the maintenance of non-influenza acute care. Contingency plans should address potential staff shortages, adjust triage systems, and implement mortuary management procedures as needed. 20. Surge capacity planning should be conducted in advance for various scenarios, with predetermined procedures for mobilizing staff on short notice. This ensures that health systems can respond effectively to increased demands during emergencies.
